subject: EU AI Act: Risk tiering, synthetic eval plan, and deployment constraints
messages:
From: Eleni Papadopoulos <eleni.p@helioshealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helioshealth.com
Date: 2027-04-18T13:12:00Z
Subject: Clarification on EU AI Act tiering + synthetic datasets for eval

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the overview yesterday. Our regulatory team has two follow-ups for the RFP: one on how Redwood maps models and deployments to EU AI Act risk tiers, and another on your approach for synthetic datasets used in evaluation/regression. Specific asks: 

- Can you confirm whether we can restrict model deployment to EU-only regions (and what operational constraints that introduces)?
- How do you classify model variants (e.g., instruction-tuned vs. base) when assigning a risk tier?
- For synthetic datasets used in evaluation or regression tests, what guarantees do you provide about provenance, non-inference of PII, and reproducibility?
- Do you retain any KV cache or request-level traces that could be considered data retention risk under EU laws?

Ideally we need answers and a short plan we can include in the RFP response by COB Monday. I can loop in procurement if there are contract implications.

Best,
Eleni
Eleni Papadopoulos
Head of AI Governance, Helios Health
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Eleni Papadopoulos <eleni.p@helioshealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T17:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarification on EU AI Act tiering + synthetic datasets for eval

Eleni — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise eval plan (redwood-eu-aiact-eval-plan.pdf) that covers our risk-tiering methodology, regional control options, and synthetic data guardrails. High level here to get you started: 

- EU-only deployment: supported. We provision model-serving pools in EU regions and can enforce a routing policy that prevents traffic from leaving the region. This is available both on Hosted and Redwood Private (VPC) modes; Private gives you additional network controls and KMS/HSM integration.

- Risk-tiering approach: we combine three signals: intended use (customer-provided), model capability profile (measured perf on targeted tasks), and output impact (severity/likelihood heuristics). We score models and variants independently — e.g., an instruction-tuned intermediate-size model used in clinical summarization would be higher-tier than a base model used for low-risk classification. We include the scoring rubric in section 2 of the attached.

- Synthetic datasets for eval: we generate synthetic data via prompt-based augmentation and model-driven synthesis, but we maintain a provenance ledger (hashes + generation recipe) for each synthetic sample. We run membership-inference and PII-detection automated checks before including synthetic examples in a benchmark. Reproducibility: recipes and seed states are captured in our eval harness so results can be re-run deterministically by our teams and provided to customers under NDA.

- KV cache and traces: default Hosted mode keeps ephemeral KV caches only for active sessions and they are purged based on inactivity thresholds; we do not persist request-level raw inputs beyond retention windows set per-customer. For EU-only retention and stricter requirements we recommend Redwood Private + configured retention policies and KMS-backed encryption.

Next steps: Neha (technical) and Vivek (contracts) are CC'd for any technical specifics or contract language. Happy to do a 30-min walkthrough tomorrow — propose 11:00 CEST / 10:00 BST?

Regards,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Eleni — quick technical follow-up and clarifications (quoting Soojin below for context):

> - Synthetic datasets for eval: we generate synthetic data via prompt-based augmentation and model-driven synthesis, but we maintain a provenance ledger (hashes + generation recipe) for each synthetic sample.

A few specifics we typically provide in gating docs / RFP annex: 

- Provenance & Non-PII assurance: every synthetic sample is stored with a provenance object: generator model + prompt template + random seed + deterministic post-processing. We run two automated checks: a regex+NER PII detector and a held-out membership-inference check against customer-supplied PII seed lists (if provided under NDA). If either check hits, that sample is excluded.

- Reproducibility & tooling: our eval harness (attached as an export in the spreadsheet) records the full pipeline: data synthesis step, augmentation passes, seed state, tokenizer/version, and runtime containers. This makes reproduction possible in a Private deployment or by our team.

- Sampling & regression coverage: we recommend stratified sampling across prompt templates, length bins, and failure modes captured in your acceptance criteria. For high-risk use cases (EU high-tier), we run both unit-level regressions (per-prompt) and end-to-end scenario regressions, and keep a rolling window of N latest runs for statistical trend analysis.

- KV cache: technical detail — KV caches are local to the GPU worker runtime and are cleared following session termination; ephemeral metrics (latency counters, token counts) are aggregated and stored as anonymized telemetry. If you need zero-ephemeral persistence we can disable telemetry collection and enforce immediate cache eviction at the edge in Private deployments.

Attached: synthetic-dataset-proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet with example recipes and reproducibility checklist). Happy to expand any section for inclusion in your RFP appendix.

-Neha
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Soojin and Neha — this is very helpful. Procurement has two contract questions before we include this in the RFP: 

1) Can you commit to an explicit geographic carve-out clause (EU-only processing) in the Data Processing Addendum?
2) For the synthetic dataset provenance and tests, can you add a warranty clause that samples furnished to Helios will not contain customer-identifiable data (and a remediation path if issues are found)?

Also procurement is asking for your latest contract redlines (we previously received v1). Can you send v2 with the EU-processing language and the warranty language for the synthetic dataset tests? We will route that to legal.

If possible, please return redlines by EOD Tuesday; otherwise we may need an interim statement to include in the RFP.

Appreciate the quick turn.
Eleni
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Eleni Papadopoulos <eleni.p@helioshealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarification on EU AI Act tiering + synthetic datasets for eval

Eleni — forwarding our redlines and a short summary of the proposed contract language (attached: redlines_contract_v2.docx). Summary: 

- EU-only processing: we will commit to EU-only processing for the contracted Helios workloads in Hosted mode with a routing and geo-fence policy; for full legal guarantees we recommend Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC) where we include a geographic carve-out in the DPA. Clause locations: DPA §3.2, Service Annex A.

- Synthetic dataset warranty: we will provide a contractual representation that synthetic evaluation datasets supplied by Redwood will have passed our PII/membership checks and that, to the best of Redwood's knowledge following commercially reasonable efforts, they will not contain customer-identifiable data. If a breach is discovered, our remediation path includes immediate dataset quarantine, 30-day remediation plan, and notification to Helios as per DPA breach timelines. We are unable to provide an insurer-backed absolute warranty (we do provide indemnity limits tied to standard enterprise terms).

- Signature: we can generate a DocuSign packet for the redlines (link: DocuSign:0x9f3e) or share via secure Drive (see link in email header).

If that aligns, I can route the DocuSign to procurement once you confirm. Happy to join a call with legal if they want to walk through the exact phrasing.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
